item.title: Chinese police chief meets Vietnamese counterpart
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong on Tuesday met with Luong Tam Quang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese Minister of Public Security, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wang, also a member of the Secretariat of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, expressed the hope that both sides will fully implement the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries. He called for sustained efforts to deepen practical cooperation in law enforcement and security, with a focus on safeguarding political security and combating telecom and online fraud. Quang voiced the willingness to strengthen solidarity and coordination with the Chinese side to achieve further progress in law enforcement and security cooperation.

item.title: Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Carney is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Canada to further advance their new strategic partnership, he added. Xi said China and Canada should build on the current momentum to enhance political mutual trust and steadily build the right perception of each other's development path and policy intent, deepen understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and settle differences and disagreements. The two countries should better align efforts to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade, energy, agriculture and finance, and expand cooperation in emerging areas including the green economy, e-commerce and the digital economy, in order to better harness each other's strengths and achieve win-win outcomes, he said. He called for deeper people-to-people exchanges and more exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, tourism, science, technology and youth as well as at subnational levels. He also proposed closer coordination to jointly practice true multilateralism, uphold the authority of the United Nations and the multilateral trading system, and build a more just and equitable global governance system. Carney said that bilateral relations have been on the right track of development since the launch of the Canada-China new strategic partnership during his meeting with Xi early this year. The two countries can fully advance and deepen cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, Carney said. Canada will work with China to pursue stronger cooperation in trade, investment, new energy, agricultural products, artificial intelligence, tourism and other areas, reduce the list of irritants, and expand the list of cooperation, he said. Canada stands ready to strengthen coordination with China to advance cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, uphold multilateralism, promote free trade, and contribute to stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region and the world, Carney added.

item.title: Xi says to boost China-Papua New Guinea ties to new heights
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea (PNG) to enhance political mutual trust and strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, advancing the development of bilateral relations to new heights. China has always regarded PNG as a trustworthy good friend and good partner, Xi said while meeting with PNG Prime Minister James Marape in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Marape is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that the PNG government adheres to the one-China principle and takes concrete actions to support China's efforts to safeguard territorial integrity and national reunification, Xi said it is a just act in keeping with the trend of history. Xi stressed that China stands ready to work with PNG to strengthen exchanges on governance and development experience, better synergize high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and PNG's Connect PNG Program and other strategies, and deepen cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, agriculture and fisheries, and energy and minerals. China is also ready to explore new avenues of cooperation in the digital economy, financial services, green energy, science and technology to help PNG achieve sustainable development, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen coordination within multilateral fora such as the United Nations and the APEC, uphold international fairness and justice, expand cooperation in tackling climate change and protecting the marine environment, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi noted. China is a good friend and the most important partner of PNG, Marape said. Over the past 50 years of diplomatic ties, PNG has consistently adhered to the one-China principle, firmly supported China in safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and resolutely backed China's efforts to achieve national reunification and advance national rejuvenation. PNG highly appreciates China's important role in guiding international affairs, supports the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi Jinping, and stands ready to strengthen multilateral coordination with China to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and promote prosperity and stability in the Asia-Pacific region, he said.

item.title: Xi says China-Vietnam top-level exchanges inject positive energy into regional peace, development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday met with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. In recent years, the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries have maintained close exchanges and reached important consensus on building a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance, Xi said. This has helped advance bilateral relations and injected positive energy into regional peace and development, Xi added. The Vietnamese leader is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi expressed willingness to deepen experience sharing with Vietnam, firmly support each other, and strengthen exchanges on self-supervision and self-governance of the parties, so as to ensure continuous progress in both countries' socialist causes and national development. "As comrades and brothers, China and Vietnam must stand together and weather the storms," Xi said. Xi also underscored the importance of enhancing mutual trust and solidarity, deepening all-round cooperation, jointly safeguarding peace and stability, and advancing shared development and prosperity. The two sides should properly manage maritime differences and steadily advance maritime cooperation, Xi said. Xi called on China and Vietnam to strengthen coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation and Lancang-Mekong cooperation, and to fulfill their duties as successive hosts of APEC in 2026 and 2027, respectively. Noting that the Vietnamese side views China as its most important strategic support, Lam said that, amid the current complex international situation, his country stands ready to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to support the development of both countries. Lam also pledged to work with China to safeguard maritime stability. As the next APEC host, Vietnam will build on the outcomes of APEC "China Year" and continue efforts to advance Asia-Pacific cooperation, the Vietnamese leader added.

item.title: Xi says advancing China-Mexico ties significant to Global South in seeking strength through unity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that advancing China-Mexico relations to new heights, across broader areas and in greater depth is of great significance to implementing their respective national development strategies and supporting the Global South in seeking strength through unity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. China is ready to work with Mexico to steer bilateral relations toward high-quality development, promote the building of an Asia Pacific that is prosperous, stable, open, interconnected, universally beneficial, inclusive, united and mutually supportive, as well as a more just and equitable global governance system, and contribute to world peace and common development, Xi added.

item.title: Xi says China ready to further develop ties with Peru
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday said China is ready to work with Peru to elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. China has remained Peru's largest trading partner and largest export destination country for 12 consecutive years, Xi said while meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Fujimori is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Xi also noted that the protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement took effect officially about two weeks ago, and the Chancay Port, built with the participation of Chinese enterprises, has given a strong boost to economic and trade cooperation between Asia and Latin America.

item.title: Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that he is ready to work with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast to strengthen strategic guidance, keep to the right direction, and jointly draw a blueprint for the growth of bilateral relations, so as to support the development and prosperity of the two countries. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with Kast in Shenzhen. The Chilean president is in the southern Chinese city to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. The most valuable experience is that the two sides respect each other, treat each other as equals, and pursue win-win outcomes, he said. As this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Chile comprehensive strategic partnership and the 20th anniversary of the entry into force of the China-Chile Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral relations have reached an important juncture for building on past achievements and forging ahead into the future, Xi said.

item.title: Chinese premier urges China, ASEAN to stand united, overcome distractions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Monday that in a turbulent and complex world, China and ASEAN should stand united, overcome distractions and work together to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Li made the remarks during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that over the past five years, the world has witnessed a growing trend of unilateralism and protectionism, while geopolitical conflicts have flared up one after another. Against this backdrop, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative improvements, with cooperation mechanisms further consolidated and connectivity steadily enhanced, he said. The extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons, Li said. He stressed that both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development. These experiences and lessons are a valuable asset shared by both sides and should be upheld and put to full use over the long term, Li said. Five years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed that China and ASEAN work together to build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, Li said, adding that both China and ASEAN countries cherish the culture of family and are geographically close and bound by strong people-to-people ties. The profound bonds forged over generations should not, and will not, be affected by temporary events or circumstances, he said. Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea, Li said. He also called for promoting regional development and prosperity, stressing the need for both sides to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity," in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules. The premier said China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation next year, advance "AI+" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development. Li also called for improving the well-being of the people, voicing China's readiness to continue to contribute to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation with ASEAN in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, maternal and child health, so as to promote sustainable development in the region. Commending the fruitful outcomes achieved over the five years since the establishment of the ASEAN-China comprehensive strategic partnership, leaders of ASEAN countries expressed readiness to strengthen strategic communication and political mutual trust with China, fully implement the ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and deepen cooperation in areas including economy and trade, connectivity, AI, clean energy, digital economy and combating transnational crime. They thanked China for its consistent support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture and its commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes. They also expressed the hope for an early conclusion of the COC in the South China Sea, jointly safeguarding regional peace and stability, and building an ASEAN-China community with a shared future. It was announced during the meeting that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec. 1, 2026, and 2027 has been designated as the Year of AI cooperation. Outcome documents were released, covering the 5th anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, energy partnership building, and deeper forestry cooperation. Full Text: Remarks by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the 29th China-ASEAN Summit

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area Updated: November 16, 2026 18:37Xinhua ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary. Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries. Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said. During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) off to a good start.
